name: Clean Harbors, Inc.
moat_justification: Permitted hazardous-waste incinerator/landfill/TSDF network is effectively un-replicable and cradle-to-grave liability makes customers sticky, with PFAS/regulatory demand tailwinds; but ROIC proxy has run only 10.6-12.6% in recent years (7.3-8.2% in 2020-21) and gross margin is flat near 31% (30.7-32.0% band, FY2020-25), so returns are modestly above the cost of capital, not wide-moat level. CAP 9.8 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED: the only cash tag filed for the latest fiscal year is the combined cash + restricted-cash total and no restricted-cash tag separates it — net debt is UNDERSTATED by the restricted amount (escrow / collateral / regulatory); check the balance sheet before trusting HIGH_NET_DEBT's absence
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 4.5x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Quality permitted hazardous-waste franchise, moat 6/10 — but at $320.06 it does not come close to clearing 15% (weighted IRR 6.24%, IV@15 $89.05; clears 15% only near $89).
moat_for: Largest permitted North American hazardous-waste disposal network (incinerators, secure landfills, TSDFs) — new permits effectively unobtainable
Cradle-to-grave customer liability under environmental law makes vendor switching risky and sticky
Regulatory tightening (incl. PFAS destruction) routes non-deferrable demand to permitted capacity
Integrated transport + disposal network: routing/cost advantage and ES/SKSS cross-selling
Proven pricing: utilization/volume growth with ES margin expansion
moat_against: ROIC proxy only ~10.6-12.6% recently and gross margin flat near 31% — pricing power is bounded
SKSS re-refining economics ride volatile base-oil spreads
WM/Republic/Veolia and regional rivals contest less permit-bound services; growth partly bought with debt-funded M&A
